title: Milestone 2 — let the dependency recover between attempts
subtitle: Baseline: milestone 1. Outcome rules are retained; timing becomes a caller choice. Every proposed wait has an observable admission boundary.

lanes.title: D1 · Give recovery time
body: Application authors want to reduce immediate repeated pressure on a recovering dependency while retaining bounded retry control.
A1 seeks this outcome. Successful and final failed calls must return promptly.

lanes.title: D2 · Schedule eligible retries
body: Today: every admitted retry starts immediately.
Proposed: wait before an admitted retry using a caller-selected doubling schedule; leaving delay unset retains immediate retries.

lanes.title: D3 · Double, then cap
body: First wait = initial_delay. Each later wait doubles up to max_delay. The example requests 0.1, 0.2, 0.25 seconds.
Constrains D2; supplies recovery time without unbounded requested waits.

lanes.title: D4 · Wait only between calls
body: No wait before the first call, after success, after an unrelated failure, or after the final allowed failure.
Constrains D2; protects prompt delivery and the existing attempt bound.

lanes.title: D5 · Retain caller outcomes
body: The first call counts. Return the original successful value; propagate the original unrelated or exhausted exception.
Constrains D2. A waiting dependency failure is not an operation failure to retry.

lanes.title: A1 · Application author / viewer
body: Today: chooses attempts and eligible exceptions.
Proposed: also chooses initial and maximum delay; can supply a waiting function to observe the schedule.

lanes.title: A2 · Retry Kit
body: Today: decides eligibility and count.
Proposed: after those decisions, requests the full next delay from A4 and then invokes A3. Owns schedule progression, not the passage of time.

lanes.title: A3 · Report operation
body: Callback responsibility remains caller-owned.
Today’s example becomes ready on read 3. Proposed example becomes ready on read 4, exposing all three requested waits.

lanes.title: A4 · Waiting function
body: Default provider: time.sleep. Injectable provider: caller-supplied wait(seconds).
Receives seconds and returns before the next call begins. Failures escape; they do not consume retry attempts.

lanes.title: A5 · Synchronous process
body: Viewer, callback, and library share one call stack. Production waits block that thread.
No scheduler, background task, async protocol, or external service is introduced.

lanes.title: C1 · RetryPolicy
body: Today: validates attempts and exception types.
Proposed: also validates finite nonnegative delay values. Positive initial delay requires a maximum at least as large.

lanes.title: C2 · retry executor
body: Today: immediately loops after an eligible failure.
Proposed: check remaining attempts, take one interval, call wait for positive intervals, then loop. The operation alone stays inside the matching try block.

lanes.title: C3 · Interval iterator
body: No scheduling component exists today.
Proposed: produce the initial interval and capped doublings. Each invocation owns its iterator. Iterative capped growth avoids constructing large exponents.

lanes.title: C4 · Report rehearsal
body: Today: immediate 3/2/1-call scenarios.
Proposed: append a 4-read recovery case and a 4-read exhaustion case; record requested waits while using real time.sleep.

lanes.title: C5 · Public surface
body: Existing imports and two policy arguments remain usable. New timing fields have defaults that retain immediate retries.
No separate public scheduler or decorator is added.

lanes.title: I1 · Timing configuration
body: RetryPolicy adds initial_delay=0.0 and max_delay=None. Values are finite int/float seconds; bool is invalid.
Positive initial_delay requires max_delay >= initial_delay.

lanes.title: I2 · retry(..., wait=...)
body: Today: callback and policy only.
Proposed: keyword-only wait defaults to time.sleep. Existing calls remain valid. Validate callable dependencies before invoking the operation.

lanes.title: I3 · intervals(policy)
body: Iterator yields one delay for each admitted retry. Does not call an operation or sleeper.
The executor consumes it only after an eligible nonfinal failure.

lanes.title: I4 · wait(seconds)
body: Executor supplies a positive number of seconds; provider returns or raises. Zero intervals bypass the provider.
An exception here propagates unchanged even when retry_on includes its class.

lanes.title: I5 · operation() / result
body: Caller-owned callback still returns T or raises. Only callback exceptions are classified for retries.
Success and failure object identity, attempt counting, and cancellation behavior remain.

lanes.title: S1 · Immutable timing settings
body: Today: policy holds attempts and exception tuple.
Proposed: add normalized delay floats and optional maximum. Construction rejects invalid values before work starts.

lanes.title: S2 · Invocation progress
body: Today: one attempt ordinal.
Proposed: ordinal plus a fresh interval iterator. Advancing the schedule cannot add an operation call or bypass the attempt limit.

lanes.title: S3 · Next interval
body: Iterator starts at initial_delay. After yielding, its next value becomes min(2 * current, max_delay).
Zero stays zero; reaching the cap stays capped. State is not stored on the reusable policy.

lanes.title: S4 · Current exception
body: The active eligible failure remains available through waiting. A final failed attempt re-raises immediately, before schedule consumption.
No retry history or global waiting state is stored.

lanes.title: S5 · Recorded waits
body: A test list records requested intervals without sleeping. The consumer records the same requests while actually sleeping.
Requested waits are evidence of scheduling, not a guarantee of exact wall-clock duration.

lanes.title: V1 · Configuration unit checks
body: Reject negative/nonfinite delays, bool, missing positive-delay cap, and cap below initial delay.
Retain all milestone 1 policy and exception validation checks.

lanes.title: V2 · Public scheduling scenario
body: Four calls succeed after waits [0.1, 0.2, 0.25]. A recording function replaces sleeping.
Assert the ordered call/wait event stream, not just the final returned value.

lanes.title: V3 · Interval unit checks
body: Verify doubling, cap saturation, zero delay, repeated use, and very large finite delays.
Failure signal: a value exceeds the cap or a reused invocation starts with an advanced interval.

lanes.title: V4 · Stop / dependency checks
body: Four failed calls have only three waits and preserve failure #4. Success/unrelated/final failures do not wait.
A selected sleeper error escapes once; it never restarts the operation.

lanes.title: V5 · Consumer and wheel
body: Today: subprocess asserts three immediate cases.
Proposed: also assert delayed recovery/exhaustion outputs. Run the installed wheel consumer with the real waiting provider.
